title: Dynamic Response of Steel Column with Attached Mass Subjected to Blast Loading
content: This study develops a mathematical model to predict the lateral deflection and stress response of an axially loaded steel Timoshenko beam that carries an attached rigid mass and is subjected to blast loading. By utilizing Lagrange's equations alongside the assumed-mode method, the governing equations are derived for a Timoshenko beam featuring uniformly distributed viscous damping under a lateral pressure wave generated by a surface explosion. The model is subsequently used to conduct a parametric investigation into how explosive charge mass, stand-off distance, attached mass, beam length, and section type affect the structural response and factor of safety. The results demonstrate that structural safety is primarily governed by the explosive charge mass and stand-off distance, whereas the investigated variations in static axial loading and beam length have a comparatively limited influence. Ultimately, the proposed formulation provides an efficient analytical framework for estimating the blast-induced response and critical safe distances of steel columns.
